fields.doc:
Monotonic tick bumped by `on_visible` so a page re-entry ALWAYS re-delivers
the current projection to the observer, even when the projected VO is
unchanged. modify_state dedups equal states (PartialEq); without this, a
header that settled to content_visible=false while the shell was invisible
(the true→false hide never reached the view) would never re-notify on return
→ the view stayed visibly stale ("Cross Nx" on a simple account). Cross-
platform: both Kotlin and iOS observers pick this up (the raw setStateObserver
has no StateFlow-style replay-on-resubscribe). Native reads state() and never
renders this field.

name: compute_amount_by_percent
doc:
R13 — V1 `getAmountCal` percent branch port (Double). Returns
the percent-derived amount string. When `state.balance` is
`None` returns empty string (V1 fall-back — no balance loaded).

V1 ref: `SpotStopDoubleFragment.kt:700-748`. The full V1 body
has TWO branches per (side × symbol_type) combo; this Rust port
covers the 4 main combos exactly:

- BUY + BASE:
* tp_market_limit==true (i.e. TP=market) → `getNewMarketMaxSize`
(which itself returns `available / (max_trigger * 1.05)`)
* else canBorrow → `maxSize`; !canBorrow → `maxSize -
loanMaxSize`
- BUY + QUOTE:
* canBorrow → `available`; !canBorrow → `available -
loanAvailable`
- SELL + BASE:
* canBorrow → `available`; !canBorrow → `available -
loanAvailable`
- SELL + QUOTE:
* canBorrow → `maxSize`; !canBorrow → `maxSize -
loanMaxSize`

The percent × amount multiply is performed via plain f64 (V1
uses `BigDecimal.divide(100).multiply(amt)` — fastnum-free
approach is acceptable for the percent-derived hint; the
authoritative submit-side numeric is recomputed on the RPC).

Pure counterpart `PureHisPosDetailsActivity`.

The three key/value rows on that page use their OWN labels and embed the unit INSIDE the
value, unlike the history list where the unit lives in the column header:

| Row | Native page label (HisPosDetailsActivity.kt:208,211,214) | Native page value |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `pr_demotrade_text_order_liquidation_trigger_price` | `"{fmtPrice(triggerPx, HALF_UP).first} {.second}"` |

page keys. Do not "align" them back to the list-row labels.

variants.name: SubmitFailed
variants.doc:
Emitted ONLY when BOTH consent writes failed (`recorded_any == false`).

This is an OBSERVABLE CONTRACT — do not widen it. A PARTIAL success (exactly one mechanism
recorded) emits [`Self::Acknowledged`] instead, because the failed mechanism's store still
reads unsigned, so the show-condition re-presents the disclosure on the next Buy/Sell, which
is the established fail-safe outcome. Native's handling depends on that split: routing a
partial success here would surface a failure for an acceptance that DID record.

Note also what this event does NOT imply: the presentation is not terminated. The `submit()`
failure branch leaves `finished` unset and does not `unregister`, and restores
`is_confirm_enabled` from `is_checked`, so a retry after a total failure is genuinely live.

bubble. Computes the "≈ {symbol}{value} ({ccy})" valuation from the
CURRENT price (passed by the caller) × the Rust-held quote-ticker last ×
the Rust-held USD→local fiat rate, then formats / rounds / groups /
prefixes it exactly like the state-driven producer.

The rate (`state.usd_to_local_rate`), fiat symbol (`state.local_fiat_symbol`)
and ticker last (`state.quote_ticker_last`) are read from Rust state — NOT
from params, per the contract. The only param is the live price string.
Empty price falls back to the InstContext ticker.last (same as the
producer) so the bubble can preview against the current ticker before
the user types.

ADDITIVE: as of 2026-06-11 (Image #6 problem 1) the rate / symbol /
quote-ticker this query reads are now PRIMARILY self-fetched in Rust —
the fiat rate + symbol from `CurrencyRateManager`
(`populate_fiat_rate_from_rust`, driven by on_visible / start / resume)
and the quote-ticker last from the session's cup-tickers-3s stream
(`QuoteTickerSubscription`). The native-push producers (`update_fiat_rate`
/ `update_price_bubble`) are retained for Android compatibility and act
as a secondary writer of the same state fields. `has_focus` remains a
native-only signal (UI focus Rust cannot observe). Pure read — no state
mutation.

NOTE: a new `#[uniffi::export]` method requires UniFFI binding regen
before Kotlin / iOS can call it; the Rust side compiling is the gate here.
